maintenance_impact.evidence: The writer's alloc/open/drain/free invariants now span cmds/record.c and utils/kernel.c, and cleanup already diverged: the moved error loop drops free and reset_tracing_files that the owner previously performed. Any buffer or offline-cpu change must coordinate two files, and the duplicated probe can silently diverge from find_symname; repair restores durable module ownership.

development_plausibility.evidence: Functions move verbatim with their doc comments and callbacks; includes are correctly added (dirent.h, stdlib.h, tracefs.h for get_tracing_file); helpers use real project idioms (xcalloc, pr_dbg, snprintf paths) and take the caller's writer_data, matching local C practice. Helper-at-callsite growth during tuning, hardening and feature work reads as ordinary repository evolution, with no task-shaped scaffolding.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The prompt matches the diff exactly, names each cluster's displaced responsibility, and rules out realistic near-misses: no withered halves, withdraw the load_kernel_files exposure, no lingering command-local copies, clean dead duplicates. It fixes the preservation boundary (entry points, formats, CLI, warning behavior) and defuses the environmentally failing kernel_tracefs test, decisively preventing wrong direction and incomplete cleanup.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Five purposes need distinct code-supported decisions: restoring the setup fragment (declarations, call-site removal), the open loop (reconstructing error cleanup, open-then-toggle ordering), teardown (drain/close/free placement versus save and the enabled guards), reader relocation (includes, static-versus-public linkage), and probe deduplication (verify equivalence, revert to find_symname).

localization_burden.evidence: Scope requires combining record.c's lifecycle, kernel.c's withered halves and the kernel.h exposure, plus comparing graph.c's copy against symbol.c's original; the file-local scandir callbacks travel only indirectly via scandir. Plausible exclusions exist: record.c's legitimate module calls (setup/start/finish/record_kernel_tracing) and the untouched static load_current_kernel beside the exposed loader. No second layered indirection.

repair_coordination.evidence: Two coupled rules: array ownership and release timing. Restoring allocation inside setup_kernel_tracing changes what start_kernel_tracing's error path must free, and restoring the drain block interacts with the injected enabled guards. A natural partial repair that re-completes the owners but leaves record.c's helper calls double-allocates, then double-drains/frees only at session teardown after ordinary sessions work.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: The best uniform operation, relocating displaced functions back into the owner module, cleanly repairs only the reader setup/teardown pair with its callbacks and linkage exposure — roughly three of ten locations (20–40%). The three writer stages need per-site merging into withered owners (declarations, error cleanup, guard interplay), and the graph duplicates must be deleted and re-pointed to find_symname instead.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Two hidden failure paths: asymmetric error cleanup (the moved loop omits freeing families and reset_tracing_files) and guard/state interplay in the withered owners. A partial repair keeping close_kernel_traces while restoring owner teardown double-frees at finish after normal sessions work — stages that each succeed alone — and the suite cannot catch it since kernel_tracefs fails environmentally.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
